title: Tassili n'Ajjer rock art
summary: Tassili n'Ajjer is a vast sandstone plateau in southeastern Algeria holding one of the world's most significant concentrations of prehistoric rock art, with over 15,000 recorded paintings and engravings. Created across successive cultural periods from early Holocene hunter-gatherers through pastoral cattle herders and later horse and camel eras, the rock art chronicles dramatic ecological changes, documenting a lush, savanna-like Green Sahara teeming with wildlife such as hippopotamuses, elephants, and crocodiles before aridification produced the modern desert.

uncertainty.note: Earliest rock art estimates range from c. 10,000 BCE to 6,000 BCE (OSL dates around 12,000–9,000 years ago); production continued into the early centuries CE.

The earliest art is thought to be about 12,000 years old, with the majority between 10,000 and 9.000 years old, based on OSL dating of associated sediments. Some 15,000 paintings and engravings have been identified and documented

importance.justification: The rock art of Tassili n'Ajjer provides the most extensive visual record of prehistoric human cultures, pastoral development, and environmental shifts across the Green Sahara.
